Vice Director of the Transmission Office

units.zh: 列傳五十七
units.en: Biographies 57
units.literal: Biographies 57

units.zh: 郝浴子林楊素蘊郭琇
units.en: Hao Yu; his son Lin; Yang Suyun; Guo Xiu
units.literal: Hao Yu; his son Lin; Yang Suyun; Guo Xiu

units.zh: 郝浴，字雪海，直隸定州人。
units.en: Hao Yu, styled Xuehai, came from Dingzhou in Zhili.
units.literal: Hao Yu, whose style name was Xuehai, was a native of Dingzhou in Zhili.

units.zh: 少有志操，負氣節。
units.en: From youth he was ambitious and unyielding in principle.
units.literal: In youth he had lofty resolve and bore himself with moral integrity.

units.zh: 順治六年進士，授刑部主事。
units.en: He took his jinshi degree in Shunzhi 6 and was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

units.zh: 八年，改湖廣道御史，巡按四川。
units.en: In year 8 he became Huguang circuit censor with a tour of inspection in Sichuan.
units.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to censor of the Huguang circuit and sent to inspect Sichuan.

units.zh: 時張獻忠將孫可望、李定國等降明，為桂王將，據川南為寇，師討之，郡縣吏率軍前除授，恣為貪虐。
units.en: Sun Kewang, Li Dingguo, and other Zhang Xianzhong lieutenants had gone over to the Ming and fought for the Prince of Gui from bases in southern Sichuan. While imperial forces pressed them, local officials were often commissioned in the field and abused their power without restraint.
units.literal: At that time Sun Kewang, Li Dingguo, and other generals of Zhang Xianzhong had surrendered to the Ming and served the Prince of Gui, holding the south of Sichuan as bandits; as the army campaigned against them, prefectural and county officials were mostly appointed on the spot ahead of the troops and indulged in greed and cruelty.

units.zh: 浴至，嚴約束，廉民間疾苦，將吏始斂跡。
units.en: Yu tightened discipline, investigated popular distress, and the military and civil staff finally curbed their excesses.
units.literal: When Yu arrived he imposed strict discipline, inquired into the people's hardships, and the officers and clerks at last restrained themselves.

units.zh: 九年，平西王吳三桂與固山額真李國翰分兵復成都、嘉定、敘州、重慶。
units.en: In year 9 Wu Sangui, Prince Who Pacifies the West, and Li Guohan, gushan ejen, led separate columns to retake Chengdu, Jiading, Xuzhou, and Chongqing.
units.literal: In the ninth year the Prince Who Pacifies the West, Wu Sangui, and the gushan ejen Li Guohan divided their forces and recovered Chengdu, Jiading, Xuzhou, and Chongqing.

units.zh: 已而兩路兵俱敗，三桂退駐綿州。
units.en: Soon both armies were beaten and Sangui fell back to Mianzhou.
units.literal: Before long both columns were defeated and Sangui withdrew to camp at Mianzhou.

units.zh: 浴在保寧監臨鄉試，可望將數万人薄城，浴飛檄邀三桂，激以大義，謂「不死於賊，必死於法」。
units.en: Yu was in Baoning overseeing the civil examinations when Kewang approached with tens of thousands of men. He fired off urgent messages to Sangui, appealing to honor: "Either I die fighting the bandits, or I die under the code."
units.literal: Yu was at Baoning supervising the provincial examination when Kewang brought tens of thousands of men to press the city; Yu sent urgent dispatches summoning Sangui and roused him with the call of duty, saying, "If I do not die at the hands of the rebels, I shall die by the law."

units.zh: 踰月，三桂乃赴援，可望等引去。
units.en: After a month Sangui finally marched to relieve the city, and Kewang withdrew.
units.literal: After more than a month Sangui at last came to the rescue and Kewang and the others withdrew.

units.zh: 浴在圍城中，上詔詢收川方略，疏言：「秦兵苦轉餉，川兵苦待哺，故必秦不助川而後秦可保；
units.en: During the siege the court asked how Sichuan might be recovered. Yu wrote: "Shaanxi armies are worn down moving grain, and Sichuan armies are worn down waiting for rations. Shaanxi can only stay secure if it stops feeding Sichuan;
units.literal: While Yu was in the besieged city the throne issued an edict inquiring about strategy to recover Sichuan; he memorialized, saying, "Qin troops suffer from transporting supplies, and Sichuan troops suffer from waiting to be fed; therefore Qin must not aid Sichuan before Qin itself can be preserved;

units.zh: 川不冀秦助而後川可圖。
units.en: and Sichuan can only be won if it does not count on help from Shaanxi.
units.literal: and Sichuan must not look to Qin for aid before Sichuan can be taken in hand.

units.zh: 成都地大且要，灌口一水，襟帶三十州縣。
units.en: Chengdu is broad and vital: the Guankou channel alone ties together more than thirty prefectures and counties.
units.literal: Chengdu is vast and strategic; the single watercourse at Guankou girds more than thirty prefectures and counties.

units.zh: 若移兵成都，照籍屯田，開耕一年，可當秦運三年。
units.en: Shift the army to Chengdu, register households for garrison farms, and one year's planting would replace three years of grain shipped from Shaanxi.
units.literal: If troops were moved to Chengdu and garrison farming were carried out according to household registers, one year of cultivation could equal three years of transport from Qin.

units.zh: 所難者牛種，倘令土司出牛，撫臣與立券，豐年還其值，當無不聽命。
units.en: Oxen and seed are the hard part—but if chieftains lent cattle and the governor issued notes redeemable in good years, they would comply.
units.literal: The difficulty lies in oxen and seed; if native chiefs were ordered to supply oxen and the governor drew up bonds to repay their value in good harvest years, they would surely obey.

units.zh: 嘉定據上游，饒茶、鹽，令暫易穀種，則牛、種俱不難辦也。
units.en: Jiading upstream is rich in tea and salt; allow temporary barter for grain and seed there, and both cattle and seed become manageable.
units.literal: Jiading lies on the upper reaches and abounds in tea and salt; if grain and seed were temporarily exchanged there, both oxen and seed would be easy to obtain.

units.zh: 臣故謂開屯便。
units.en: That is why I urge garrison farming.
units.literal: Your servant therefore holds that opening garrison farms is advantageous.

units.zh: 川所患者滇寇也，滇寇所恃，不過皮兜、布鎧、鳥銃、濩刀，善於騰山踰嶺。
units.en: Sichuan's scourge is the Yunnan rebels, who rely on little more than leather shields, cloth armor, muskets, and broadswords—and on moving like goats over mountains.
units.literal: What afflicts Sichuan is the Yunnan bandits; what the Yunnan bandits rely on is no more than leather shields, cloth armor, muskets, and broadswords, and skill at leaping mountains and crossing ridges.

units.zh: 蜀中土官土兵，其技尤嫻於此。
units.en: Shu's native officers and militia are even better at it.
units.literal: The native officials and native troops of Shu are even more skilled in this.

units.zh: 若拔其精銳為前茅，以滿洲驍騎為後勁，疾雷迅霆，賊必鳥獸散。
units.en: Take their best as the van, Manchu horse as the hammer behind, and strike like thunder—the rebels would break like startled game.
units.literal: If their picked men were taken as vanguard and Manchu crack cavalry as rear strength, like sudden thunder and lightning the bandits would surely scatter like birds and beasts.

units.zh: 臣故謂用土兵便。」
units.en: That is why I urge using native troops."
units.literal: Your servant therefore holds that employing native troops is advantageous."

units.zh: 上以其言可採，下部議。
units.en: The emperor found this worth pursuing and sent it to the ministries.
units.literal: The emperor judged his words worth adopting and referred them to the ministries for deliberation.

units.zh: 部議謂戰守事當聽三桂主之，遂報寢。
units.en: The ministries ruled that war and defense were Sangui's to decide, and the proposal died there.
units.literal: The ministries held that matters of campaigning and defense should be left to Sangui's decision, and the memorial was reported shelved.

units.zh: 浴又言：「土賊投誠，給劄授官，恣行劫掠為民害。
units.en: Yu added: "Bandit chiefs who submit receive warrants and posts, then loot at will and plague the people.
units.literal: Yu also said, "Native bandits who surrender are given warrants and offices and then freely plunder, harming the people.

units.zh: 請嗣後原歸伍者歸伍，原為民者，令有司造冊編丁，免牛租，除雜派，就熟地開徵，俾有定額。」
units.en: Let those who were soldiers return to the ranks; let those who were civilians be registered, freed from ox rent and extra levies, and taxed on cultivated land at fixed rates."
units.literal: I ask that hereafter those who were originally soldiers return to the ranks, and those who were originally commoners be registered by the local authorities, exempted from ox rent and miscellaneous levies, and assessed on cultivated land so that fixed quotas may be set."

units.zh: 疏議行。
units.en: This memorial was approved and carried out.
units.literal: The memorial was deliberated and approved.

units.zh: 三桂入四川，浸驕橫，部下多不法，憚浴嚴正，輒禁止沿路塘報。
units.en: Once Sangui was in Sichuan he grew arrogant; his men broke the law freely. They feared Yu's rigor and repeatedly cut off courier reports along the road.
units.literal: When Sangui entered Sichuan he grew increasingly arrogant; many of his subordinates acted unlawfully, and fearing Yu's severity they repeatedly blocked relay reports along the route.

units.zh: 浴上言：「臣忝司朝廷耳目，而壅閼若此，安用臣為？」
units.en: Yu protested: "I am supposed to be the court's eyes and ears—if information is choked off like this, what am I here for?"
units.literal: Yu memorialized, saying, "Your servant is charged to serve as the court's eyes and ears, yet if obstruction is such as this, of what use is your servant?

units.zh: 及保寧圍解，頒賞將士，三桂以冠服與浴，浴不受。
units.en: After Baoning was relieved and rewards were handed out, Sangui offered Yu ceremonial dress; Yu refused.
units.literal: When the siege of Baoning was lifted and rewards were issued to officers and soldiers, Sangui offered Yu robes and cap, but Yu would not accept.

units.zh: 疏言：「平賊乃平西王責。
units.en: He wrote: "Crushing the rebels is the Prince's duty.
units.literal: In a memorial he said, "Pacifying the bandits is the Prince Who Pacifies the West's duty.

units.zh: 臣司風憲，不預軍事，而以臣預賞，非黨臣則忌臣也。」
units.en: I oversee discipline and took no part in the fighting—yet I am rewarded. That flatters me or it marks me for suspicion."
units.literal: Your servant oversees discipline and did not take part in military affairs; to include your servant in the reward is either to court your servant or to begrudge your servant."

units.zh: 因陳三桂擁兵觀望狀，三桂深銜之。
units.en: He went on to describe Sangui hoarding troops and holding back. Sangui never forgave him.
units.literal: He also described Sangui's holding troops and watching from the sidelines, and Sangui deeply resented him.

units.zh: 浴劾永寧總兵柏永馥臨陣退縮，廣元副將胡一鵬驕悍不法，並命奪官逮治。
units.en: Yu impeached Bai Yongfu, Yongning commander, for retreating in battle, and Hu Yipeng, Guangyuan vice commander, for arrogance and abuse of power; both were stripped of rank and arrested.
units.literal: Yu impeached Yongning regional commander Bai Yongfu for shrinking back in battle and Guangyuan vice commander Hu Yipeng for arrogance and lawlessness, ordering both stripped of office and arrested for trial.

units.zh: 降將董顯忠等以副將銜題授司道，恣睢虐民，浴复疏劾，改原職。
units.en: Surrendered generals such as Dong Xianzhong had been promoted to circuit posts with vice-commander titles and tyrannized the people. Yu impeached them again and they were reduced to their former ranks.
units.literal: The surrendered generals Dong Xianzhong and others had been nominated at vice-commander rank for provincial posts and acted tyrannically, harming the people; Yu again memorialized against them and they were returned to their former ranks.

units.zh: 三桂嗾顯忠等入京陳辨，浴坐鐫秩去。
units.en: Sangui sent Xianzhong and the others to Beijing to plead their case, and Yu was demoted and dismissed.
units.literal: Sangui incited Xianzhong and the others to go to the capital to plead their case, and Yu was demoted in rank and removed from office.

units.zh: 十一年，大學士馮銓、成克鞏、呂宮等交章薦浴，三桂乃摭浴保寧奏捷疏有「親冒矢石」語，指為冒功，論劾，部議當坐死，上命寬之，流徙奉天。
units.en: In year 11 Grand Secretaries Feng Quan, Cheng Kegong, and Lü Gong recommended Yu in turn. Sangui seized on Yu's Baoning victory report and the phrase "personally braved arrow and stone," accused him of false credit, and impeached him. The ministries called for death; the emperor commuted the sentence to exile in Fengtian.
units.literal: In the eleventh year Grand Secretaries Feng Quan, Cheng Kegong, Lü Gong, and others jointly memorialized to recommend Yu; Sangui then seized from Yu's Baoning victory memorial the phrase "personally braved arrows and stones," charged him with claiming false merit, and impeached him; the ministries held he deserved death, but the emperor ordered leniency and banished him to Fengtian.

units.zh: 大學士馮銓、成克鞏、呂宮皆以薦浴罣吏議。
units.en: Feng Quan, Cheng Kegong, and Lü Gong were censured for having backed him.
units.literal: Grand Secretaries Feng Quan, Cheng Kegong, and Lü Gong were all implicated in official censure for recommending Yu.

units.zh: 浴至戍所，益潛心義理之學，嗜孟子及二程遺書，以「致知格物」顏其廬，刻苦厲志。
units.en: At his place of exile he threw himself into moral philosophy, devouring Mencius and the Cheng brothers, naming his lodge "Investigate Things, Extend Knowledge," and living with austere purpose.
units.literal: When Yu reached his place of exile he devoted himself ever more to the study of moral principle, cherished Mencius and the surviving works of the Cheng brothers, and inscribed his lodge with "extending knowledge through investigating things," disciplining himself with bitter resolve.

units.zh: 康熙十年，聖祖幸奉天，浴迎謁道左，具陳始末，上為動容，慰勞良久。
units.en: In Kangxi 10 the emperor visited Fengtian. Yu met him by the road, told his whole story, and moved the emperor to long and heartfelt consolation.
units.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi the Sacred Ancestor visited Fengtian; Yu met him by the roadside and set forth the whole story in detail; the emperor was moved and comforted him at length.

units.zh: 十二年，三桂反，尚書王熙、給事中劉沛先薦浴，為部議所格。
units.en: In year 12 Sangui rebelled. Minister Wang Xi and supervising secretary Liu Pei recommended Yu first, but the ministries blocked it.
units.literal: In the twelfth year Sangui rebelled; Minister Wang Xi and supervising secretary Liu Pei first recommended Yu, but the recommendation was blocked in ministry deliberation.

units.zh: 十四年，侍郎魏象樞复疏言：「浴血性過人，才守學識，臣皆愧不及。
units.en: In year 14 Vice Minister Wei Xiangshu wrote again: "Yu's courage is extraordinary; in talent, integrity, and learning I cannot match him.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year Vice Minister Wei Xiangshu again memorialized, saying, "Yu surpasses others in native courage; in talent, integrity, and learning your servant is ashamed to fall short of him.

units.zh: 使在西蜀操尺寸之權，豈肯如羅森輩俯首從逆？
units.en: Had he held even a little power in western Shu, would he have bowed to rebels like Luo Sen?
units.literal: Had he held even a measure of authority in western Shu, how could he have bowed his head in rebellion like Luo Sen and his kind?

units.zh: 臣子立朝，各有本末。
units.en: Every official's story has a beginning and an end.
units.literal: When ministers serve at court, each case has its beginning and end.

units.zh: 當日參浴者三桂也，使三桂始終恭順，方且任以腹心。
units.en: The man who attacked Yu then was Sangui—and if Sangui had stayed loyal, the court would still have trusted him with everything.
units.literal: The one who impeached Yu then was Sangui; had Sangui remained always respectful and obedient, he would still have been trusted as a confidant.

units.zh: 浴一書生耳，即老死徙所，誰復問之？
units.en: Yu was only a scholar. He could have died in exile unnoticed.
units.literal: Yu was only a scholar; even if he died of old age in exile, who would ask after him?

units.zh: 今三桂叛矣，天下無不恨三桂，即無不憐浴。
units.en: Now Sangui has rebelled. The empire hates Sangui—and pities Yu.
units.literal: Now Sangui has rebelled; under heaven none do not hate Sangui, and none do not pity Yu.

units.zh: 浴當三桂身居王爵，手握兵柄，不畏威，不附勢，致為所仇。
units.en: When Sangui held a princely title and an army, Yu neither feared him nor curried favor—and Sangui made him an enemy.
units.literal: When Yu faced Sangui, who held a princely title and grasped military power, he did not fear authority and did not cling to power, and thus became Sangui's enemy.

units.zh: 三桂之所仇，正國家之所取，何忍棄之？」
units.en: Whom Sangui hated is exactly whom the throne should want. How can we abandon him?"
units.literal: Whom Sangui hated is precisely whom the state should take up; how can we bear to cast him aside?"

units.zh: 上乃召浴還，复授湖廣道御史。
units.en: The emperor recalled Yu and restored him as Huguang circuit censor.
units.literal: The emperor then summoned Yu back and again appointed him censor of the Huguang circuit.

units.zh: 時陝西提督王輔臣叛應三桂，浴疏言：「大兵進剿平涼，宜於西安、潼關用重兵屯駐，以待策應。
units.en: Wang Fuchen, Shaanxi commander, had joined the rebellion. Yu wrote: "As the main force moves on Pingliang, hold Xi'an and Tong Pass with strong garrisons ready to support it.
units.literal: At that time Shaanxi provincial commander Wang Fuchen rebelled in support of Sangui; Yu memorialized, saying, "As the main army advances to suppress Pingliang, heavy forces should be stationed at Xi'an and Tong Pass to await coordinated action.

units.zh: 用鄖陽之兵攻興安，調河南之兵入武關，直取漢中，逆賊計日可擒。」
units.en: Send Yunyang troops against Xing'an, bring Henan troops through Wuguan straight into Hanzhong, and the rebels will fall in days."
units.literal: Use the troops of Yunyang to attack Xing'an, move Henan troops through Wuguan, and strike straight for Hanzhong; the rebel can be taken within days."

units.zh: 上然之，下其疏諸帥。
units.en: The emperor agreed and sent the plan to the field commanders.
units.literal: The emperor approved and circulated his memorial to the commanders.

units.zh: 復請禁苛徵，恤民困，止督、撫、提、鎮坐​​名題補之例。
units.en: He also urged an end to harsh exactions, relief for the distressed, and the custom by which governors and commanders filled posts by nominal nomination.
units.literal: He again asked to forbid harsh levies, relieve the people's distress, and stop the practice by which governors-general, governors, provincial commanders, and regional commanders made nominal nominations for appointments.

units.zh: 章十數上，皆中時弊。
units.en: He filed more than a dozen such memorials, each hitting a live abuse.
units.literal: He submitted more than a dozen memorials, all striking at the abuses of the time.

units.zh: 十六年，命巡視兩淮鹽政，嚴剔宿蠹，增課六十餘萬。
units.en: In year 16 he was sent to inspect Liang-Huai salt, purged entrenched corruption, and raised revenue by more than six hundred thousand taels.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year he was ordered to inspect the salt administration of the two Huai districts, rigorously rooting out long-standing corruption and increasing revenue by more than six hundred thousand taels.

units.zh: 淮、揚大饑，發倉米賑救，全活甚眾。
units.en: When famine struck Huai and Yang, he opened granaries and saved countless lives.
units.literal: When Huai and Yang suffered great famine he released granary rice for relief and saved a great multitude.

units.zh: 十七年，擢左僉都御史，遷左副都御史。
units.en: In year 17 he rose to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief, then Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief and then transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 十九年，授廣西巡撫。
units.en: In year 19 he was made governor of Guangxi.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed governor of Guangxi.

units.zh: 廣西新經喪亂，民生凋瘵，浴專意撫綏，疏陳調劑四策，請裁兵、汰馬、防要害、簡精銳；
units.en: Guangxi was just recovering from war; the people were exhausted. Yu focused on relief and proposed four reforms: cut troops, cull horses, guard key points, and keep elite units;
units.literal: Guangxi had newly suffered war and devastation; the people's livelihood was wasted; Yu devoted himself to pacification and in a memorial set forth four policies of adjustment, asking to cut troops, cull horses, guard strategic points, and select crack forces;

units.zh: 復請停鼓鑄，改米徵銀，复南寧、太平、思恩諸府縣行鹽舊制：上輒報可。
units.en: halt minting, collect grain tax in silver, and restore the old salt system in Nanning, Taiping, Si'en, and elsewhere. The emperor approved each request.
units.literal: he also asked to halt coin minting, collect grain taxes in silver, and restore the old salt regulations in Nanning, Taiping, Si'en, and other prefectures and counties; the emperor invariably approved.

units.zh: 時南疆底定，滿洲兵撤還京師。
units.en: The south was pacified and Manchu troops returned to Beijing.
units.literal: At that time the southern frontier was settled and Manchu troops were withdrawn to the capital.

units.zh: 浴疏言撫標兵不宜裁減，下部議，留其半。
units.en: Yu argued that the governor's troops should not be cut; the ministries left half in place.
units.literal: Yu memorialized that the governor's banner troops should not be reduced; after ministry deliberation half were retained.

units.zh: 又請為死事巡撫馬雄鎮、傅弘烈建祠桂林，知府劉浩、知縣周岱生為孫延齡所戕，疏請予卹。
units.en: He asked for temples at Guilin to Ma Xiongzhen and Fu Honglie, governors who died in service, and posthumous honors for Liu Hao and Zhou Daisheng, killed by Sun Yanling.
units.literal: He also asked that shrines be built at Guilin for the governors who died in service, Ma Xiongzhen and Fu Honglie, and that posthumous honors be granted to prefect Liu Hao and magistrate Zhou Daisheng, who were killed by Sun Yanling.

units.zh: 二十二年，卒官。
units.en: In year 22 he died in office.
units.literal: In the twenty-second year he died in office.

units.zh: 喪歸，士民泣送者數千里不絕。
units.en: As his coffin went home, mourners lined the road for thousands of li.
units.literal: When his coffin was borne home, scholars and commoners who wept and escorted him stretched unbroken for thousands of li.

units.zh: 初，傅弘烈以軍事急，移庫金七萬有奇、米七千餘石供餉，浴請以庫項扣抵。
units.en: Earlier, with the campaign urgent, Fu Honglie had taken more than seventy thousand taels and seven thousand shi of grain from the treasury for supplies; Yu had the treasury entries adjusted to match.
units.literal: Earlier, because military affairs were urgent, Fu Honglie had drawn more than seventy thousand taels from the treasury and more than seven thousand shi of grain for supplies; Yu asked that the treasury account be charged accordingly.

units.zh: 及卒，布政使崔維雅署巡撫，劾浴侵欺，命郎中蘇赫、陳光祖往按，如維雅言。
units.en: After his death Cui Weiya, acting governor, accused Yu of embezzlement. Investigators Su He and Chen Guangzu confirmed it.
units.literal: After Yu died, Provincial Administration Commissioner Cui Weiya acted as governor and impeached Yu for embezzlement and fraud; the throne ordered Directors Su He and Chen Guangzu to investigate on the spot, and they found as Cui had alleged.

units.zh: 部議奪官追償。
units.en: The ministries called for posthumous dismissal and repayment.
units.literal: The ministries held that his office should be posthumously stripped and restitution pursued.

units.zh: 上知浴廉，諭所動錢糧非入己，從寬免追。
units.en: Knowing Yu's integrity, the emperor ruled the funds had not enriched him personally and waived repayment.
units.literal: The emperor knew Yu was incorrupt and declared that the funds and grain he had moved had not entered his own pocket; he was leniently exempted from restitution.

units.zh: 二十五年，子林訟父冤，復原官，賜祭葬。
units.en: In year 25 his son Lin cleared his father's name; Yu's rank was restored and state funeral honors granted.
units.literal: In the twenty-fifth year his son Lin sued to clear his father's name; Yu's former rank was restored and imperial sacrifices and burial honors were granted.

units.zh: 林，字中美。
units.en: Lin, styled Zhongmei.
units.literal: Lin, whose style name was Zhongmei.

units.zh: 康熙二十一年進士，授中書科中書，歷吏部郎中，亦以廉正稱。
units.en: He took his jinshi in Kangxi 21, served as a Secretariat secretary and a Personnel director, and was likewise known for integrity.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-first year of Kangxi, was appointed a secretary in the Secretariat, served as a director in the Ministry of Personnel, and was also known for integrity.

units.zh: 累遷禮部侍郎，加尚書銜。
units.en: He rose to Vice Minister of Rites with ministerial rank.
units.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Rites and granted the nominal rank of minister.

units.zh: 致仕，卒。
units.en: He retired and died.
units.literal: He retired and died.

units.zh: 楊素蘊，字筠湄，陝西宜君人。
units.en: Yang Suyun, styled Junmei, came from Yijun in Shaanxi.
units.literal: Yang Suyun, whose style name was Junmei, was a native of Yijun in Shaanxi.

units.zh: 順治九年進士，授直隸東明知縣。
units.en: He took his jinshi in Shunzhi 9 and was made magistrate of Dongming in Zhili.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Dongming in Zhili.

units.zh: 東明當河決後，官舍城垣悉敗，民居殆盡，遺民依丘阜，僅數十家。
units.en: After the Yellow River burst its banks, Dongming's offices and walls were in ruins and almost no homes remained—only a few dozen families on the hillocks.
units.literal: Dongming lay in the aftermath of a breach in the Yellow River; government buildings and city walls were all ruined, dwellings nearly all gone, and survivors clinging to hillocks numbered only a few dozen households.

units.zh: 素蘊至，為繕城郭，招集流亡，三年戶增至萬餘。
units.en: Suyun rebuilt the walls, brought back refugees, and within three years households topped ten thousand.
units.literal: When Suyun arrived he repaired the walls and city, gathered the displaced, and within three years households increased to more than ten thousand.

units.zh: 山東群盜任鳳亭等剽掠旁郡，擾及畿南。
units.en: Shandong bandits led by Ren Fengting raided neighboring prefectures and reached the capital's southern approaches.
units.literal: Bandits in Shandong such as Ren Fengting plundered neighboring prefectures and disturbed the southern capital region.

units.zh: 素蘊設計降其渠，散其脅從。
units.en: Suyun engineered the surrender of the ringleaders and broke up their bands.
units.literal: Suyun devised a plan to induce their leaders to surrender and disperse their followers.

units.zh: 十七年，舉卓異，行取，授四川道御史。
units.en: In year 17 he was cited for excellence, brought to the capital, and made Sichuan circuit censor.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year he was cited for outstanding service, selected for capital appointment, and made censor of the Sichuan circuit.

units.zh: 疏言：「臣言官也，宜以言為事。
units.en: He wrote: "I am a censor; my job is to speak.
units.literal: In a memorial he said, "Your servant is a remonstrating official and ought to make speech his business.

units.zh: 然今天下所患，正在議論多而成功少。
units.en: Yet the realm's trouble is talk without results.
units.literal: Yet what the realm suffers from today is precisely that discussion is abundant while achievement is scarce.

units.zh: 國家建官分職，各有所事。
units.en: The state sets up offices, each with its charge.
units.literal: The state establishes offices and divides duties, each with its own charge.

units.zh: 誠使司舉劾，籌財用，任封疆，理刑獄，各舉其職，則平天下無餘事。
units.en: Let censors impeach, ministries manage revenue, governors guard the frontiers, courts judge cases—each doing its work—and pacifying the realm needs nothing more.
units.literal: If truly the censorate handled impeachment, the ministries planned revenue, frontier governors bore their commissions, and the courts judged cases, each fulfilling its role, then to pacify the realm would leave nothing undone.

units.zh: 更原皇上推誠御物，肅大閒，寬小眚，俾人人得展其才，尤端本澄源之要也。」
units.en: And let Your Majesty meet the world with sincerity, be strict in great matters and lenient in small faults, and let every man use his gifts—that is how to set things right at the source."
units.literal: I further ask that Your Majesty treat all with sincere openness, be strict in great matters and lenient in small faults, and allow every man to display his talent—this above all is the way to rectify the root and clarify the source."

units.en: (End of memorial.)
units.literal: (End of memorial.)

units.zh: 時吳三桂鎮雲南，郡縣吏得自闢署，謂之「西選」。
units.en: Wu Sangui then held Yunnan and appointed local officials at will—the "western selection."
units.literal: At that time Wu Sangui held Yunnan, and prefectural and county officials could be appointed on his own authority—this was called the "western selection."

units.zh: 漸乃題用朝臣，無復顧忌。
units.en: He soon began nominating capital officials without restraint.
units.literal: Gradually he began to nominate serving court officials, without further scruple.

units.zh: 素蘊疏言：「三桂以上湖南道胡允等十員題補雲南各道，並有奉差部員在內，深足駭異。
units.en: Suyun protested: "Sangui has nominated ten men, including Hu Yun of upper Hunan circuit, for Yunnan posts—even ministry officials on imperial commission. This is shocking.
units.literal: Suyun memorialized, saying, "Sangui has nominated ten men including Hu Yun of the upper Hunan circuit to fill the various Yunnan circuits, and among them are ministry officials on imperial commission—this is deeply shocking.

units.zh: 爵祿者人主之大柄，綱紀者朝廷之大防，柄不可移，防不可潰。
units.en: Ranks and rewards belong to the throne; discipline is the court's rampart. Neither may be given away.
units.literal: Ranks and stipends are the sovereign's great prerogative; discipline is the court's great bulwark—the prerogative must not be shifted, the bulwark must not be breached.

units.zh: 前此經略用人，特命二部不得掣肘，亦惟以軍前效用及所轄五省各官酌量題請，從未聞敢以他行省及現任京官坐缺定銜者也。
units.en: When the frontier commissioner appointed men, the ministries were told not to interfere—but only for men who had proved themselves in the field or within his five provinces. No one had ever filled vacancies in other provinces or capital posts from afar.
units.literal: When the frontier commissioner earlier appointed men, the two ministries were specially ordered not to obstruct him, yet this was only to weigh merit at the front and officials within the five provinces under his charge; never was it heard that he dared fix ranks for vacancies in other provinces or for serving capital officials.

units.zh: 且疏稱求於滇省既苦索駿無從，求於遠方又恐叱馭不速，則湖南、四川距雲南猶近，若京師、山東、江南相去萬里，不知其所謂遠者更在何方？
units.en: His memorial says Yunnan yielded no men and distant provinces might arrive too late—yet Hunan and Sichuan are near. If Beijing, Shandong, and Jiangnan are "too far," what place is farther still?
units.literal: Moreover his memorial says that seeking men in Yunnan proved fruitless and seeking from afar feared they would not arrive in time—yet Hunan and Sichuan are still near Yunnan; if the capital, Shandong, and Jiangnan lie ten thousand li away, where can the "far" he speaks of be?

units.zh: 皇上特假便宜，不過許其就近調補。
units.en: The discretion Your Majesty granted was only for local transfers.
units.literal: The special discretionary power granted by Your Majesty was no more than permission to transfer and fill posts nearby.

units.zh: 若盡天下之官，不分內外，不論遠近，皆可擇而取之，何如歸吏部銓授，尤為名正言順。
units.en: If every post in the empire, near or far, civil or military, may be filled at will, better return the power to the Ministry of Personnel, where it belongs.
units.literal: If officials throughout the realm, without distinction of inner or outer service or of distance, may all be chosen at will, how much better to return appointment to the Ministry of Personnel by regular selection—that would be all the more proper in name and right in fact.

units.zh: 縱或云、貴新經開闢，料理乏人，諸臣才品為籓臣所素知，亦宜請旨令吏部簽補；
units.en: Even if newly opened Yunnan and Guizhou lack administrators and Sangui knows these men's talents, he should still ask the throne and let the Ministry of Personnel appoint them;
units.literal: Even if Yunnan and Guizhou have newly been opened and lack men to administer them, and the talents of these officials are well known to the frontier lord, it is still fitting to request an edict and have the Ministry of Personnel sign and fill the posts;

units.zh: 乃徑行擬用，不亦輕名器而褻國體乎？
units.en: to appoint them directly—is this not to cheapen office and insult the state?
units.literal: to proceed directly with proposed appointments—is this not to treat titles lightly and profane the dignity of the state?

units.zh: 人臣忠邪之分，起於一念之敬肆。
units.en: Loyalty and treason in a minister begin with a single thought of reverence or arrogance.
units.literal: The division between loyal and treacherous ministers begins in a single thought of reverence or presumption.

units.zh: 籓臣敭歷有年，應知大體。
units.en: The frontier lord has held his post for many years; he should know what propriety demands.
units.literal: The frontier lord has held his fief for many years and ought to understand the larger principles.

units.zh: 此舉為封疆計，未必別有深心，然防微杜漸，當慎於幾先。
units.en: This move may have been meant for the frontier alone, not some hidden plot—but small wrongs grow large; one must act at the first sign.
units.literal: This act was for the sake of the frontier and need not imply any other deep design, yet to guard against the subtle and stop the gradual, one must be cautious at the first sign.

units.zh: 祈申飭籓臣，嗣後惟力圖進取，加意撫綏，一切威福大權，俱宜禀自朝廷，則君恩臣誼兩盡其善。」
units.en: I ask that the frontier lord be warned: hereafter let him press forward and soothe his people, and let every grant of power come from the court—so sovereign and subject both do what is right."
units.literal: I beg that the frontier lord be sternly admonished: hereafter let him strive only for advance and give added care to pacification; all great powers of authority and favor should be reported to and received from the court—then sovereign grace and ministerial duty will both be fulfilled at their best."

units.zh: 疏下部。
units.en: The memorial went to the ministries.
units.literal: The memorial was sent to the ministries.

units.zh: 十八年，聖祖即位，輔臣柄政，出素蘊為川北道。
units.en: In year 18 the emperor took the throne; the chief ministers were in charge and sent Suyun to the northern Sichuan circuit.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year the Sacred Ancestor ascended the throne; the chief ministers held power and transferred Suyun out to the northern Sichuan circuit.

units.zh: 三桂見素蘊前奏，惡之，具疏辨，並摘「防微杜漸」語，謂意含隱射，語伏危機。
units.en: Sangui read Suyun's earlier memorial, took offense, and replied at length, seizing on "guard against the subtle and stop the gradual" as a veiled threat.
units.literal: Sangui, seeing Suyun's earlier memorial, hated him and submitted a detailed rebuttal, seizing on the phrase "guard against the subtle and stop the gradual," claiming the meaning carried hidden insinuation and the wording concealed menace.

units.zh: 詔責素蘊回奏，素蘊言：「防微杜漸，古今通義。
units.en: The throne ordered Suyun to respond. He said: "To stop trouble at the first sign is a principle as old as government itself.
units.literal: An edict ordered Suyun to answer; Suyun said, "To guard against the subtle and stop the gradual is a universal principle of ancient and modern times.

units.zh: 臣但期籓臣每事盡善，為聖世純臣，非有他也。」
units.en: I only wanted the frontier lord to do everything well and be a loyal servant of a sage reign—nothing more."
units.literal: Your servant only hoped the frontier lord would do everything well and be a pure minister of this sage age—there was no other intent."

units.zh: 下部議，坐素蘊巧飾，當降調，罷歸。
units.en: The ministries found him guilty of clever evasion, ordered demotion, and sent him home.
units.literal: After ministry deliberation Suyun was found guilty of clever evasion, liable to demotion, and dismissed to return home.

units.zh: 居十年，三桂反。
units.en: Ten years later Sangui rebelled.
units.literal: After ten years at home, Sangui rebelled.

units.zh: 尚書郝惟訥、冀如錫，侍郎楊永寧交章請起用，惟訥詞尤切，略言：「素蘊首劾三桂，雲當防微杜漸。
units.en: Ministers Hao Weina and Ji Ruxi and Vice Minister Yang Yongning asked that he be recalled. Weina wrote most urgently: "Suyun was the first to attack Sangui and warned that trouble must be stopped at the first sign.
units.literal: Ministers Hao Weina and Ji Ruxi and Vice Minister Yang Yongning jointly memorialized to request his reinstatement; Weina's words were especially urgent, saying in summary, "Suyun was the first to impeach Sangui, declaring that one must guard against the subtle and stop the gradual.

units.zh: 在當日反狀未形，似屬杞憂。
units.en: Then rebellion had not yet shown itself—it looked like needless worry.
units.literal: At the time the signs of rebellion had not yet appeared, and it seemed idle worry.

units.zh: 由今觀之，則素蘊先見甚明，且為國直陳，奮不自顧，其剛腸正氣，實有大過人者！
units.en: Looking back, his foresight is plain. He spoke straight for the state and risked everything—his integrity truly stood above other men!
units.literal: Viewed from today, Suyun's foresight was very clear; moreover he spoke plainly for the state and strove without regard for himself—his upright spirit truly surpassed others!

units.zh: 亟宜優錄。」
units.en: He should be honored and restored at once."
units.literal: He should urgently be favored and recorded for service."

units.zh: 乃命發湖廣軍前，以原品用。
units.en: He was sent to the Huguang front at his former rank.
units.literal: He was then ordered dispatched to the Huguang front to serve at his former rank.

units.zh: 會丁父憂，服闋，乃赴軍前。
units.en: He was in mourning for his father; when mourning ended he reported to the army.
units.literal: He happened to be in mourning for his father; when the mourning period ended he went to the front.

units.zh: 總督蔡毓榮題補湖廣提學道，部議當以現辦軍務參議道題補。
units.en: Governor-General Cai Yurong nominated him for the Huguang education circuit; the ministries said he should fill the military affairs post he was already handling.
units.literal: Governor-General Cai Yurong nominated him to fill the Huguang education circuit; the ministries held he should be nominated to the military affairs deliberation circuit he was then handling.

units.zh: 康熙十七年，題補下荊南道。
units.en: In Kangxi 17 he was appointed to the lower Jingnan circuit.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi he was nominated and appointed to the lower Jingnan circuit.

units.zh: 時襄陽總兵楊來嘉、副將洪福等叛應三桂。
units.en: Xiangyang commander Yang Laijia, vice commander Hong Fu, and others had joined the rebellion.
units.literal: At that time Xiangyang regional commander Yang Laijia, vice commander Hong Fu, and others rebelled in support of Sangui.

units.zh: 大軍運餉，自襄至房、保路險C7，舟車不通，歲調襄陽、安陸、德安三郡丁夫擔負，餉苦不繼。
units.en: Supplying the army from Xiangyang to Fang and Bao meant a road too steep for carts or boats. Each year laborers from Xiangyang, Anlu, and De'an were pressed to carry grain on their backs, and rations still ran short.
units.literal: The main army transported supplies; from Xiangyang to Fang and Bao the route was perilously steep, boats and carts could not pass, and each year corvée laborers from the three prefectures of Xiangyang, Anlu, and De'an were levied to carry on their backs, so that supplies sorely failed to keep up.

units.zh: 素蘊訪知穀城有小溪可通舟，乃按行山谷開餉道，由是水運通利，省丁夫什九，軍乃無乏。
units.en: Suyun found a stream at Gucheng that could take boats, surveyed the hills, and opened a water route—cutting corvée by nine-tenths and keeping the army fed.
units.literal: Suyun learned that Gucheng had a small stream navigable by boat; he then surveyed the valleys and opened a supply route, whereby water transport became convenient, nine-tenths of the corvée was saved, and the army was no longer short.

units.zh: 遷山西提學道。
units.en: He was transferred to the Shanxi education circuit.
units.literal: He was transferred to the Shanxi education circuit.

units.zh: 二十四年，任滿，薦舉擢通政司參議，累遷順天府尹。
units.en: In year 24, when his term ended, he was promoted to Transmission Office vice director and then metropolitan governor of Shuntian.
units.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when his term ended, he was recommended and promoted to Vice Director of the Transmission Office, and in succession was made metropolitan governor of Shuntian.

units.zh: 二十六年，授安徽巡撫。
units.en: In year 26 he was made governor of Anhui.
units.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed governor of Anhui.

units.zh: 會歲饑，上疏請賑。
units.en: Famine struck; he memorialized for relief.
units.literal: Famine struck that year and he memorialized requesting relief.

units.zh: 甫拜疏，即檄州縣開倉賑給，全活甚眾。
units.en: Before the memorial even arrived he had ordered granaries opened; countless lives were saved.
units.literal: Hardly had he submitted the memorial when he ordered the prefectures and counties to open granaries and give relief, saving a great multitude.

units.zh: 尋調湖廣巡撫。
units.en: He was soon transferred to governor of Huguang.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to governor of Huguang.

units.zh: 夏逢龍亂初定，脅從尚眾，人情恇擾，一夕數驚。
units.en: Xia Fenglong's rebellion had just ended; many who had been forced to follow were still at large, and the people panicked at every rumor.
units.literal: The rebellion of Xia Fenglong had just been settled; those coerced into following were still numerous, hearts were fearful and unsettled, and in a single night there were several alarms.

units.zh: 素蘊首嚴告訐之禁，反側以安。
units.en: Suyun strictly forbade malicious informing, and unrest subsided.
units.literal: Suyun first imposed a strict ban on informers, and the restless were thereby pacified.

units.zh: 二十八年，大旱，疏請蠲免武昌等屬三十二州縣錢糧，上遣戶部郎中舒淑等會督撫勘災。
units.en: In year 28 a great drought struck. He asked remission of taxes for thirty-two counties around Wuchang. The emperor sent Shu Shu of the Revenue Ministry and others to survey the damage with the provincial leadership.
units.literal: In the twenty-eighth year there was great drought; he memorialized requesting remission of taxes and grain for thirty-two prefectures and counties under Wuchang and elsewhere; the emperor sent Ministry of Revenue Director Shu Shu and others to join the governor-general and governor in surveying the disaster.

units.zh: 舒淑至武昌，素蘊適患暑疾，令布政使於養志從總督丁思孔往勘。
units.en: When Shu Shu reached Wuchang, Suyun was ill with summer fever and sent Commissioner Yu Yangzhi with Governor Ding Sikong to inspect.
units.literal: When Shu Shu reached Wuchang, Suyun happened to be ill from summer heat and ordered Provincial Administration Commissioner Yu Yangzhi to accompany Governor Ding Sikong on the survey.

units.zh: 尋稱病乞休，上疑其託疾，奪官。
units.en: He soon asked to retire on grounds of illness; the emperor thought he was feigning and dismissed him.
units.literal: Soon he claimed illness and asked to retire; the emperor suspected he was feigning sickness and stripped him of office.

units.zh: 命甫下而素蘊已卒。
units.en: The order had barely gone out when Suyun died.
units.literal: The order had scarcely been issued when Suyun had already died.

units.zh: 先是，湖北郡縣疾苦最甚者，如沔陽、江陵、漢陽、嘉魚濱江地陷未蠲賦額，咸寧、黃陂、景陵谷折，江夏、崇陽、武昌、通城、漢陽、漢川、雲夢、孝感、應城穀田科重，監利一年兩賦，為民害數十年。
units.en: Among Huguang's worst abuses: Mianyang, Jiangling, Hanyang, and Jiayu still taxed land swallowed by the river; Xianning, Huangpi, and Jingling used short measures; Jiangxia, Chongyang, Wuchang, Tongcheng, Hanyang, Hankou, Yunmeng, Xiaogan, and Yingcheng bore crushing levies on good land; Jianli paid two taxes in one year—decades of injury to the people.
units.literal: Earlier, among the worst hardships in Huguang prefectures and counties were these: Mianyang, Jiangling, Hanyang, and Jiayu, where riverbank land had subsided but tax quotas were not remitted; Xianning, Huangpi, and Jingling, where grain was assessed at broken measure; Jiangxia, Chongyang, Wuchang, Tongcheng, Hanyang, Hankou, Yunmeng, Xiaogan, and Yingcheng, where fertile fields bore heavy levies; and Jianli, which paid two assessments in one year—harms to the people for decades.

units.zh: 素蘊得其實，條為兩疏。
units.en: Suyun verified the facts and drafted two memorials.
units.literal: Suyun obtained the facts and set them forth in two memorials.

units.zh: 未及上而病革，口授入遺疏，曰：「此疏行，吾目瞑矣！」
units.en: Before he could submit them he was dying. He dictated a final memorial: "When this is enacted, I can close my eyes!"
units.literal: Before he could submit them his illness turned critical; he dictated them into a deathbed memorial, saying, "When this memorial is carried out, my eyes may close!"

units.en: (End of memorial.)
units.literal: (End of memorial.)

units.zh: 郭琇，字華野，山東即墨人。
units.en: Guo Xiu, styled Huaye, came from Jimo in Shandong.
units.literal: Guo Xiu, whose style name was Huaye, was a native of Jimo in Shandong.

units.zh: 康熙九年進士。
units.en: He took his jinshi in Kangxi 9.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Kangxi.

units.zh: 十八年，授江南吳江知縣。
units.en: In year 18 he was made magistrate of Wujiang in Jiangnan.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed magistrate of Wujiang in Jiangnan.

units.zh: 材力強幹，善斷疑獄。
units.en: He was forceful and decisive in difficult cases.
units.literal: He was forceful and capable and skilled at deciding doubtful cases.

units.zh: 徵賦行版串法，胥吏不能為奸。
units.en: He collected taxes by the plate-and-tally method, leaving clerks no room for fraud.
units.literal: In collecting taxes he used the plate-and-tally method, so clerks could not practice fraud.

units.zh: 居官七年，治行為江南最。
units.en: After seven years his record was judged the best in Jiangnan.
units.literal: After seven years in office his administration was rated the best in Jiangnan.

units.zh: 二十五年，巡撫湯斌薦琇居心恬淡，蒞事精銳，請遷擢。
units.en: In year 25 Governor Tang Bin praised his calm integrity and sharp administration and asked for his promotion.
units.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Governor Tang Bin recommended Xiu as calm in mind and sharp in affairs, and asked that he be promoted.

units.zh: 部議以琇徵賦未如額，寢其奏，聖祖特許之，行取，授江南道御史。
units.en: The ministries blocked the nomination because tax collection had fallen short, but the emperor overruled them, brought Xiu to the capital, and made him Jiangnan circuit censor.
units.literal: The ministries held that Xiu had not met his tax quota and shelved the memorial, but the Sacred Ancestor specially approved it; he was selected for capital appointment and made censor of the Jiangnan circuit.

units.zh: 時河督靳輔請停濬下河，築高家堰重堤，清丈堤外田畝以為屯田，謂可增歲收百餘萬。
units.en: Grand Canal Director Jin Fu wanted to stop dredging the lower reach, build up the Gaojia Weir dikes, and turn dike-side fields into garrison farms, claiming a million taels in added revenue.
units.literal: At that time Grand Canal Director Jin Fu asked to halt dredging of the lower river, build heavy dikes at the Gaojia Weir, and survey fields outside the dikes for garrison farms, claiming annual revenue could increase by more than a million taels.

units.zh: 巡撫於成龍議不​​合，上令尚書佛倫往勘，主輔議。
units.en: Governor Yu Chenglong disagreed. Minister Folun was sent to inspect and sided with Jin Fu.
units.literal: Governor Yu Chenglong disagreed; the emperor ordered Minister Folun to investigate on the spot and he upheld Fu's plan.

units.zh: 下九卿覈奏，尚書張玉書、左都御史徐乾學力言屯田擾民。
units.en: The Nine Ministers reviewed the plan. Zhang Yushu and Xu Qianxue argued forcefully that garrison farms would harm the people.
units.literal: The matter was referred to the Nine Ministers for review; Minister Zhang Yushu and Left Censor-in-Chief Xu Qianxue strongly argued that garrison farms disturbed the people.

units.zh: 二十七年，琇疏劾輔治河無功，偏聽幕客陳潢阻濬下河。
units.en: In year 27 Xiu impeached Jin Fu for failing to control the river and letting his secretary Chen Huang block dredging of the lower reach.
units.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Xiu memorialized impeaching Fu for achieving nothing in river control and blindly following his secretary Chen Huang in blocking dredging of the lower river.

units.zh: 上御乾清門，召諸大臣，下琇疏，令會同察議。
units.en: The emperor met the ministers at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, circulated Xiu's memorial, and ordered a joint inquiry.
units.literal: The emperor held court at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, summoned the ministers, circulated Xiu's memorial, and ordered joint investigation and deliberation.

units.zh: 尋輔入覲，復召諸大臣與議。
units.en: When Jin Fu came to court the ministers were summoned again for deliberation.
units.literal: Soon Fu came to audience and the ministers were again summoned to deliberate with him.

units.zh: 琇申言屯田害民，輔坐罷，而擢琇僉都御史。
units.en: Xiu again argued that garrison farms harmed the people. Jin Fu was dismissed and Xiu was made Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: Xiu again declared that garrison farms harmed the people; Fu was dismissed from his post, and Xiu was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 大學士明珠柄政，與餘國柱比，頗營賄賂，權傾一時，久之為上所覺。
units.en: Grand Secretary Mingzhu ruled with Yu Guozhu, took bribes freely, and dominated the court until the emperor noticed.
units.literal: Grand Secretary Mingzhu held power, paired with Yu Guozhu, and engaged considerably in soliciting bribes; his authority dominated the age, until in time the emperor perceived it.

units.zh: 琇疏劾明珠與國柱結黨行私，詳列諸罪狀，並及佛倫、傅拉塔與輔等交通狀，於是明珠等降黜有差。
units.en: Xiu impeached Mingzhu and Guozhu for faction and corruption, listed their crimes in detail, and exposed collusion by Folun, Fulata, and Jin Fu. Mingzhu and the others were demoted.
units.literal: Xiu memorialized impeaching Mingzhu and Guozhu for forming a faction and pursuing private ends, listing their crimes in detail, and also exposing the collusion of Folun, Fulata, and Fu and others; thereupon Mingzhu and the rest were demoted to varying degrees.

units.zh: 琇直聲震天下。
units.en: Xiu's reputation for integrity resounded across the empire.
units.literal: Xiu's reputation for integrity shook the realm.

units.zh: 遷太常寺卿，再遷內閣學士。
units.en: He became Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then Grand Secretariat academician.
units.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and then again to Grand Secretariat academician.

units.zh: 二十八年，复遷吏部侍郎，充經筵講官，擢左都御史。
units.en: In year 28 he became Vice Minister of Personnel, lectured at the Classics Colloquium, and was made Left Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was again transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel, served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 疏劾少詹事高士奇與原任左都御史王鴻緒植黨為奸，給事中何楷、修撰陳元龍、編修王頊齡依附壞法，士奇等並休致回籍。
units.en: He impeached Junior Mentor Gao Shiqi and former Censor-in-Chief Wang Hongxu for forming a corrupt clique, with He Kai, Chen Yuanlong, and Wang Xuling as their allies. Shiqi and the others were sent home in retirement.
units.literal: He memorialized impeaching Junior Mentor Gao Shiqi and former Left Censor-in-Chief Wang Hongxu for forming a clique to do evil; supervising secretaries He Kai, compiler Chen Yuanlong, and editor Wang Xuling attached themselves and corrupted the law; Shiqi and the others were all retired and sent home.

units.zh: 未幾，御史張星法劾山東巡撫錢鎯貪黷，鎯奏辨，因及琇嘗致書囑薦即墨知縣高上達等，卻之，遂挾嫌使星法誣劾，下法司訊。
units.en: Soon Censor Zhang Xingfa impeached Shandong Governor Qian Heng for corruption. Heng replied that Xiu had once asked him to recommend Jimo Magistrate Gao Shangda and that he had refused—so Xiu had Zhang bring false charges. The case went to the judiciary.
units.literal: Before long Censor Zhang Xingfa impeached Shandong Governor Qian Heng for greed and corruption; Heng memorialized in defense and mentioned that Xiu had once written asking him to recommend Jimo Magistrate Gao Shangda and others, which he had refused, and then bore a grudge and had Xingfa bring false charges; the case was sent to the judiciary for trial.

units.zh: 獄未具，琇疏言：「左都御​​史馬齊於會訊時多方鍛鍊，必欲實以指使誣劾罪。」
units.en: Before trial ended Xiu wrote: "Censor-in-Chief Ma Qi is fabricating evidence at the inquiry to convict me of directing a false impeachment."
units.literal: Before the case was concluded Xiu memorialized, saying, "Left Censor-in-Chief Ma Qi at the joint inquiry repeatedly forged evidence and was determined to establish the crime of directing a false impeachment."

units.zh: 詔責琇疑揣。
units.en: The emperor rebuked Xiu for suspicion and surmise.
units.literal: An edict rebuked Xiu for suspicion and surmise.

units.zh: 尋法司奏琇請託事實，當奪官。
units.en: The judiciary soon found solicitation proved and called for dismissal.
units.literal: Soon the judiciary reported that the fact of Xiu's solicitation was established and he should be stripped of office.

units.zh: 上以琇平日鯁直敢言，改降五級調用。
units.en: Knowing Xiu's usual integrity, the emperor reduced the penalty to demotion by five ranks.
units.literal: Because Xiu was normally upright and outspoken, the emperor commuted this to demotion by five ranks and reassignment.

units.zh: 二十九年，吏部推琇通政司參議，上命改令予琇休致。
units.en: In year 29 Personnel recommended him for Transmission Office vice director; the emperor ordered retirement instead.
units.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the Ministry of Personnel recommended Xiu for Vice Director of the Transmission Office; the emperor ordered instead that Xiu be granted retirement.

units.zh: 江寧巡撫洪之傑以吳江縣虧漕項，事涉琇，牒山東追琇赴質。
units.en: Jiangning Governor Hong Zhijie cited a grain-transport deficit in Wujiang involving Xiu and summoned him from Shandong to stand trial.
units.literal: Jiangning Governor Hong Zhijie, on account of a grain-transport deficit in Wujiang County involving Xiu, sent a dispatch to Shandong summoning Xiu to answer the charge.

units.zh: 時佛倫為山東巡撫，因劾琇違例逗留希進用，請奪官逮治；
units.en: Folun was then Shandong governor and impeached Xiu for lingering unlawfully in hope of office, asking that he be arrested;
units.literal: At that time Folun was governor of Shandong and therefore impeached Xiu for irregular delay in hope of reappointment, asking that his office be stripped and he be arrested for trial;

units.zh: 又劾琇世父郭爾印乃明季御史黃宗昌家奴，琇父郭景昌原名爾標，嘗入賊黨伏法，琇私改父名請誥封，應追奪。
units.en: and claimed Xiu's uncle had been a Ming censor's slave, that Xiu's father had been a bandit executed under another name, and that Xiu had falsified his father's name to obtain honors—all to be revoked.
units.literal: he also impeached Xiu on the ground that his father's elder brother Guo Eryin had been a household slave of the late-Ming censor Huang Zongchang, that Xiu's father Guo Jingchang had originally been named Erbiao and had once joined bandits and been executed by law, and that Xiu had privately changed his father's name to obtain an edict of enfeoffment—all of which should be posthumously revoked.

units.zh: 部議如所請，逮赴江寧勘治。
units.en: The ministries agreed; he was arrested and sent to Jiangning for trial.
units.literal: The ministries approved as requested and had him arrested and sent to Jiangning for investigation and trial.

units.zh: 坐侵收運船飯米二千三百餘石，事發彌補，議遣戍，詔寬之。
units.en: He was found to have taken more than twenty-three hundred shi of transport-boat rations, made restitution when exposed, and was sentenced to exile—but the emperor commuted it.
units.literal: He was found guilty of unlawfully taking more than twenty-three hundred shi of rice meant for transport boats' rations; when the matter came to light he made restitution; banishment was proposed, but an edict granted leniency.

units.zh: 三十八年，上南巡，琇迎駕德州。
units.en: In year 38 the emperor toured the south and Xiu met him at Dezhou.
units.literal: In the thirty-eighth year the emperor made a southern tour and Xiu met the imperial procession at Dezhou.

units.zh: 既還京師，諭大學士阿蘭泰等曰：「原任左都御史郭琇，前為吳江令，居官甚善，百姓感頌至今。
units.en: Back in Beijing he told Grand Secretary Arantai: "Former Censor-in-Chief Guo Xiu served Wujiang well—the people still praise him.
units.literal: After returning to the capital he told Grand Secretary Arantai and others, "Former Left Censor-in-Chief Guo Xiu, when he was magistrate of Wujiang, governed very well, and the people praise him to this day.

units.zh: 其人有膽量，可授湖廣總督，令馳驛赴任。」
units.en: He has backbone. Make him governor-general of Huguang and send him posthaste."
units.literal: The man has courage and may be appointed governor-general of Huguang; order him to take post by urgent relay."

units.zh: 琇上官，疏言：「黃州、武昌二府兵米二萬七千有奇，運給荊州、鄖陽汛地，懸隔千里，輓輸費不貲，請改折色。
units.en: On taking office Xiu wrote: "Huangzhou and Wuchang send more than twenty-seven thousand units of military grain a thousand li to Jingzhou and Yunyang garrisons at ruinous cost—let it be commuted to silver.
units.literal: When Xiu took office he memorialized, saying, "The military grain of Huangzhou and Wuchang prefectures, more than twenty-seven thousand odd, is transported to garrison posts at Jingzhou and Yunyang a thousand li away; transport costs are beyond reckoning—I ask that it be commuted to silver.

units.zh: 江夏等十三州縣有故明籓產，田瘠賦重，數倍民糧，請一律減徵。
units.en: Thirteen counties including Jiangxia still hold former Ming princely estates taxed several times heavier than common land—reduce them uniformly.
units.literal: Thirteen prefectures and counties including Jiangxia hold former Ming princely estates where the land is poor but the levy heavy, several times commoners' grain tax—I ask uniform reduction.

units.zh: 江夏、嘉魚、漢陽三縣瀕江地，水齧土陊，有賦無田者三百餘頃，請豁免。」
units.en: In Jiangxia, Jiayu, and Hanyang more than three hundred qing along the river are taxed though the land is gone—exempt them."
units.literal: In Jiangxia, Jiayu, and Hanyang, riverbank land eroded by water and soil collapse has more than three hundred qing taxed though no fields remain—I ask exemption."

units.zh: 皆允行。
units.en: All were approved.
units.literal: All were approved and carried out.

units.zh: 三十九年，入覲，因奏言：「臣父景昌，即墨縣諸生，有冊可稽。
units.en: In year 39 he came to audience and said: "My father Jingchang was a Jimo licentiate—there are records.
units.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he came to audience and memorialized, saying, "Your servant's father Jingchang was a licentiate of Jimo County and is recorded in the registers.

units.zh: 邑匪郭爾標本無妻室，安得有子？
units.en: The bandit Guo Erbiao had no wife—how could he have had a son?
units.literal: The local bandit Guo Erbiao had no wife—how could he have had a son?

units.zh: 不知佛倫何所據，誣臣並及臣父。」
units.en: On what grounds did Folun slander me and my father?"
units.literal: I do not know on what Folun relied in slandering your servant and implicating your servant's father."

units.zh: 時佛倫為大學士，上詰之，以舛錯對，命仍予誥軸。
units.en: Folun was now a grand secretary. The emperor questioned him; his answers were wrong. Xiu's honors were restored.
units.literal: At that time Folun was a grand secretary; the emperor questioned him and he answered with errors; the emperor ordered that the patent of honor still be granted.

units.zh: 琇陛辭，奏請清丈地畝，並言湖南地廣人稀，恐清丈後賦當差減。
units.en: Bidding farewell, he asked to survey land and warned that Hunan was vast and thinly settled—taxes might need to fall after survey.
units.literal: At his farewell audience Xiu asked to conduct a full land survey and said that Hunan was broad and sparsely peopled, fearing that after survey the tax quota would need considerable reduction.

units.zh: 上問：「當減幾何？」
units.en: The emperor asked: "By how much?"
units.literal: The emperor asked, "By how much should it be reduced?"

units.zh: 琇言：「當減十分之三。」
units.en: Xiu said: "By three-tenths."
units.literal: Xiu said, "It should be reduced by three-tenths."

units.zh: 上曰：「果益民，雖倍於此，亦不惜也！」
units.en: The emperor said: "If it truly helps the people, I would give twice that without hesitation!"
units.literal: The emperor said, "If it truly benefits the people, even twice that would not be regretted!"

units.zh: 尋條陳三事：一，嚴定築堤處分；
units.en: He soon proposed three reforms: first, strict penalties for dike work;
units.literal: Soon he set forth three items in order: first, strictly fix penalties for dike construction;

units.zh: 一，停造無用糧船；
units.en: second, stop building useless grain boats;
units.literal: second, halt building useless grain boats;

units.zh: 一，通融調補苗疆官吏。
units.en: third, flexible posting of officials on the Miao frontier.
units.literal: third, flexibly transfer and fill posts for Miao frontier officials.

units.zh: 又疏禁徵賦諸弊政。
units.en: He also memorialized against tax abuses.
units.literal: He also memorialized forbidding abuses in tax collection.

units.zh: 上嘉其實心除弊，並允行。
units.en: The emperor praised his sincerity and approved all.
units.literal: The emperor praised his sincere heart in removing abuses and approved all.

units.zh: 時紅苗就撫，琇陳善後之策，請頒詔敕，令勒石永遵。
units.en: The Red Miao had submitted. Xiu proposed pacification measures and asked for an edict carved in stone for permanent observance.
units.literal: At that time the Red Miao had submitted to pacification; Xiu set forth policies for aftermath, asking that an edict be promulgated and inscribed on stone for perpetual observance.

units.zh: 四十年，以病乞休，上曰：「琇病甚，思一人代之不可得，能如琇者有幾人耶？」
units.en: In year 40 he asked to retire on grounds of illness. The emperor said: "Xiu is gravely ill. I cannot find a replacement—how many men are there like him?"
units.literal: In the fortieth year he asked to retire on grounds of illness; the emperor said, "Xiu is very ill; I think of finding one man to replace him and cannot; how many men are there like Xiu?"

units.zh: 給事中馬士芳劾湖廣布政使任風厚久病，巡撫年遐齡徇庇不以聞。
units.en: Supervising secretary Ma Shifang impeached Commissioner Ren Fenghou for chronic illness; Governor Nian Xialing had shielded him and not reported it.
units.literal: Supervising secretary Ma Shifang impeached Huguang Provincial Administration Commissioner Ren Fenghou for long illness; Governor Nian Xialing shielded him and did not report it.

units.zh: 遐齡奏風厚實無病。
units.en: Xialing reported that Fenghou was not ill at all.
units.literal: Xialing memorialized that Fenghou was in fact not ill.

units.zh: 風厚入覲，上見其未衰，因曰：「任風厚若不堪任使，郭琇豈肯徇庇耶？」
units.en: Fenghou came to audience looking hale. The emperor said: "If Ren Fenghou were unfit for duty, would Guo Xiu have protected him?"
units.literal: Fenghou came to audience; the emperor saw he was not yet decrepit and therefore said, "If Ren Fenghou were unfit for service, would Guo Xiu have been willing to shield him?"

units.zh: 未幾，琇以病劇再疏求罷，仍慰留。
units.en: Soon Xiu, gravely ill, asked again to step down—and was again kept in office.
units.literal: Before long Xiu, his illness severe, again memorialized asking to be relieved, but was again comforted and retained.

units.zh: 黃梅知縣李錦催科不力，琇委員摘印。
units.en: Huangmei Magistrate Li Jin was slow in collecting taxes; Xiu sent an agent to remove him from office.
units.literal: Huangmei Magistrate Li Jin was ineffective in collecting taxes; Xiu sent an agent to remove his seal of office.

units.zh: 錦得民心，民閉城拒之，乞留錦。
units.en: Li had the people's loyalty. They shut the city gates and begged that he stay.
units.literal: Li had won the people's hearts; the people closed the city and resisted, begging that Li be kept.

units.zh: 御史左必蕃劾琇，部議當奪官，上以清丈未畢，緩之。
units.en: Censor Zuo Bifan impeached Xiu. The ministries called for dismissal, but the emperor deferred it until the land survey was done.
units.literal: Censor Zuo Bifan impeached Xiu; the ministries held he should be stripped of office, but because the land survey was not finished the emperor deferred action.

units.zh: 四十一年，鎮筸諸生李定等叩閽奏紅苗殺掠，總督、巡撫匿不以聞；
units.en: In year 41 students at Zhenqian petitioned at the palace gate that the Red Miao were killing and looting while the governor-general and governor concealed it;
units.literal: In the forty-first year students Li Ding and others of Zhenqian knocked at the palace gate to report Red Miao killings and plunder; the governor-general and governor concealed it and did not report;

units.zh: 而給事中宋駿業亦劾琇向騖虛聲，近益衰廢，持祿養癰。
units.en: and supervising secretary Song Junye impeached Xiu for chasing reputation, growing negligent, and holding office while nursing his illness.
units.literal: and supervising secretary Song Junye also impeached Xiu for having long pursued empty reputation, lately growing more negligent and holding his stipend while nursing his malady.

units.zh: 乃命侍郎傅繼祖、甘國樞，浙江巡撫趙申喬往按。
units.en: The emperor sent Vice Ministers Fu Jizu and Gan Guoshu and Zhejiang Governor Zhao Shenqiao to investigate.
units.literal: The throne then ordered Vice Ministers Fu Jizu and Gan Guoshu and Zhejiang Governor Zhao Shenqiao to investigate on the spot.

units.zh: 會琇報清丈畢，乞罷任。
units.en: Meanwhile Xiu reported the land survey complete and asked to resign.
units.literal: At the same time Xiu reported that the land survey was finished and asked to be relieved of his post.

units.zh: 上責其清丈稽延，與前奏不合，行不顧言；
units.en: The emperor rebuked him for delaying the survey, contradicting his earlier promises, and failing to match deed to word;
units.literal: The emperor rebuked him for delay in the survey, inconsistency with his earlier memorial, and acting without regard to his words;

units.zh: 並及匿報紅苗殺掠與黃梅拒命事。
units.en: and cited his concealment of Red Miao raids and the Huangmei rebellion.
units.literal: and also cited his concealing reports of Red Miao killings and plunder and the Huangmei defiance of orders.

units.zh: 琇自陳老病失察，請治罪。
units.en: Xiu confessed that age and illness had dulled his oversight and asked to be punished.
units.literal: Xiu confessed that old age and illness had caused his failure to oversee matters and asked to be punished.

units.zh: 初紅苗犯鎮筸，游擊沈長祿往剿，至大梅山，守備許邦垣、千總孫清俱陷賊，長祿私贖之歸，諱不報；
units.en: When the Red Miao attacked Zhenqian, guerrilla commander Shen Changlu marched to suppress them. At Damei Mountain garrison commander Xu Bangyuan and battalion commander Sun Qing were captured; Changlu ransomed them secretly and said nothing;
units.literal: Earlier, when the Red Miao attacked Zhenqian, guerrilla commander Shen Changlu went to suppress them; at Damei Mountain garrison commander Xu Bangyuan and battalion commander Sun Qing both fell into the bandits' hands; Changlu privately ransomed them back and concealed the matter without reporting it;

units.zh: 而副將硃紱報苗已就撫，琇據以入告。
units.en: Vice Commander Zhu Fu meanwhile reported that the Miao had submitted, and Xiu passed that report to the throne.
units.literal: while Vice Commander Zhu Fu reported that the Miao had already submitted to pacification, and Xiu reported this to the throne on that basis.

units.zh: 繼祖等勘得狀，琇與提督林本植並奪官。
units.en: Jizu and the others confirmed the facts. Xiu and Commander Lin Benzhi were both dismissed.
units.literal: Jizu and the others verified the facts on investigation, and both Xiu and Provincial Commander Lin Benzhi were stripped of office.

units.zh: 五十四年，卒。
units.en: In year 54 he died.
units.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he died.

units.zh: 尋祀鄉賢，並祀吳江名宦。
units.en: He was soon enshrined among local worthies and among Wujiang's honored officials.
units.literal: Soon he was enshrined among local worthies and also among the noted officials of Wujiang.

units.zh: 論曰：郝浴、楊素蘊秉剛正之性，抗論強籓，曲突徙薪，防禍未形，甘竄逐而不悔。
units.en: The historian comments: Hao Yu and Yang Suyun were men of stern integrity who spoke against powerful frontier lords, warned of trouble before it appeared, and accepted exile without regret.
units.literal: The historian comments: Hao Yu and Yang Suyun possessed upright and stern natures; they argued against powerful frontier lords, bent the chimney and moved the fuel, guarded against disaster before it took shape, and willingly accepted banishment without regret.

units.zh: 郭琇抨擊權相，有直臣之風，震霆一鳴，僉壬解體。
units.en: Guo Xiu struck at the powerful minister like a true remonstrator; one thunderclap and the faction crumbled.
units.literal: Guo Xiu attacked the powerful minister, bearing the manner of a straight-speaking official; one peal of thunder and the whole host fell apart.

units.zh: 蓋由聖祖已悟其奸，而琇遂得行其志。
units.en: The Sacred Ancestor had already seen through the minister's treachery, and so Xiu could act.
units.literal: This was because the Sacred Ancestor had already perceived the minister's treachery, and thus Xiu was able to carry out his purpose.

units.zh: 然以浴之廉，蒙議於身後；
units.en: Yet Yu's integrity was questioned even after death;
units.literal: Yet for Yu's integrity he was slandered after death;

units.zh: 素蘊居官愛民，不終於位；
units.en: Suyun loved the people in office but did not finish his term;
units.literal: Suyun in office loved the people but did not end his days in post;

units.zh: 琇則​​橫被誣陷，廢置十年，始獲申雪。
units.en: and Xiu was framed, cast aside for ten years, and only then vindicated.
units.literal: and Xiu was wantonly slandered and framed, set aside for ten years before his name was cleared at last.

units.zh: 得君如聖祖，猶不克善全，直道難行，不其然哉？
units.en: Even under a ruler like the Sacred Ancestor they could not come through unscathed—the straight path is hard; is that not the truth?
units.literal: Even with a ruler like the Sacred Ancestor they could not be preserved whole—how hard the straight path is to walk; is it not so?
